oneOf.description: Subscribing only.
Publishing only.
Both.

Delivery.description: A record delivered to a subscriber, live or replayed.

message_id.description: The publisher's id for the message.

published_at_ms.description: When the message was published, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

qos.description: The delivery level the publisher asked for: 0 or 1.

seq.description:
The record's position in the topic log. Consumers deduplicate by
`(topic, seq)`.

topic.description: The topic the record was published to.

ErrorCode.description:
Why a request failed. New codes may be added within a protocol version;
clients should treat an unknown code like `internal`.

oneOf.description: The frame isn't valid JSON, has an unknown `type`, or misses a field.
The request needs `auth` first. The connection is closed.
The token was invalid or expired. The connection is closed.
The username or password was wrong.
Too many failed logins; wait `retry_after` seconds.
Too many requests; wait `retry_after` seconds.
The user may not use this topic.
The account couldn't be created; `message` says why when it is safe to.
The `session_id` is empty, too long or has control characters.
The session store couldn't be reached. The connection is closed.

The server doesn't speak the requested protocol version. The
connection is closed.
The message store couldn't be reached; retry later.
The payload is longer than `Limits::max_payload_bytes`.

The topic name is empty, longer than `Limits::max_topic_bytes`, or
has control characters or the wildcard characters `+` and `#`.
Anything else went wrong on the server.
The request needs an admin account.
No account has that username.
An account with that username already exists.

heartbeat_secs.description: How often the server sends a WebSocket ping, in seconds.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
How long the server waits for anything from the client, a pong
included, before closing with `CloseCode::IdleTimeout`, in seconds.

max_inflight.description: The most QoS 1 records a subscription may have unacknowledged.

max_payload_bytes.description: The longest payload a publish may carry, in bytes.

max_topic_bytes.description: The longest topic name, in bytes.

session_expiry_secs.description: How long a durable session is kept after its last connection, in seconds.

anyOf.description: A numeric id, such as a counter.
A string id, such as a UUID.

RequestId.description:
The id a client attaches to a request, echoed in the reply.

Either a number or a string, and given back in the same form.

oneOf.description: May use every topic and the admin requests.
May use the topics its grants allow.
May subscribe to the topics its grants allow, and never publish.

RoleSpec.description: What an account may do, as admins see and set it.

topics.description:
The topic patterns it may use. Ignored for `admin`, which may use
every topic; every grant of a `readonly` account is `subscribe`.

Stalled.description: Tells a subscriber that a QoS 1 record ran out of retries.

seq.description: The record that was never acknowledged.

Subscribed.description:
Confirms a subscription and says which records are history.

The range is empty when `replay_from` is greater than `replay_to`.

replay_from.description: The first `seq` that will be sent.

replay_to.description: The newest `seq` in the log when the subscription started.

TopicGrant.description: One topic pattern and what it allows.

pattern.description: The pattern, with `+` for one level and a trailing `#` for the rest.

Truncated.description: Tells a subscriber that records it expected were trimmed.

first_available.description: The oldest `seq` still available. Delivery continues from here.

UserInfo.description: An account, as admins see it. Never includes the password or its hash.

created_at_ms.description: When it was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

enabled.description: Whether it may log in and use topics.

description: Every frame a PopSub server sends.

oneOf.description: The JWT issued for a `login`.
The account from a `register` was created.

An `auth` was accepted. On an already authenticated connection,
`auth` with a new token for the same user only refreshes the token,
and the reply's `resumed` is empty.

protocol.description: The protocol version the connection uses from now on.

resumed.description:
Topics whose stored subscriptions are being restored. Each is
followed by its own `subscribed` frame.

session_id.description: The durable session held, echoed from `auth`.

oneOf.description:
A subscription started. Records `replay_from` to `replay_to` are
history; later ones are live.

The connection no longer receives the topic. Sent in reply to
`unsubscribe`, and also without an `id` when an admin's change to the
account ended a subscription it no longer allows.
A QoS 1 publish is stored. A retried publish gets the original `seq`.

message_id.description: The id it was stored under, generated if the publish had none.

seq.description: Its position in the topic log.

oneOf.description: A record from a subscribed topic, live or replayed.
Records the subscriber expected were trimmed before it got them.

The connection's token expires soon. Send `auth` with a new token
before `expires_at_ms`, or the connection is closed with
`CloseCode::TokenExpired`.

expires_at_ms.description: When the token expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description:
A QoS 1 record ran out of retries; delivery on the topic is paused
until the client acknowledges something or subscribes again.
An account, as it stands after an admin request.
Every account, sorted by username.
An account was deleted.
A request failed.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again, for rate limits and lockouts.

id.description: The `id` of the request this answers.
